If it runs out you're knocked out and come to beside your ship - and the pirates help themselves to a tenth of your drachmas - and you lose one thing you carried (it goes on your lost list: defeating enemies may win it back). Citizens can fall to the pirates too.
- **Stamina** - the green ring outside the shield's. It runs down as you go (a full ring lasts about ten calm minutes) and three times faster in a fight - while you're being hit or firing. Eat to bring it back: any **Food & drink** good you carry (grain, figs, cheese, wine...) gives back 30, an **Energy Drink** 60 (stations sell them in their supplies; chests, lockers and pirates have some). Click it in the Field Computer's inventory, or hover it there and press 1-9 to put it on the toolbar. Its rim turns red when it's low; empty, you walk slowly and your health no longer comes back by itself. It stays as it is between landings - stock up before you go down.
- **Akrotiri** - the volcanic planet, innermost of the home system and Venus-like: basalt and ash plains and yellow sulphur flats under an orange haze, rivers and lakes of magma (you can't cross them - go round), fumaroles, obsidian spires, basalt columns and soot-blackened Greek ruins. Nobody lives there: no villages, no buildings at all - only pirates, and its beasts: twelve big, alien predators (magma behemoths, cinder stalkers, obsidian mantises, sulphur bloaters, lava serpents, vent crabs, packs of pyroclast hounds, ash wraiths, basalt golems, ember swarm queens, crater maws and fumarole titans). Every one comes for you from far off, and each has four times the health and twice the bite of the creature of the other worlds it's most like. They leave only minerals when they fall: iron ore, titanium from the tougher ones, and now and then platinum from the biggest. Its **heat** wears on you: your health comes back **half as fast** there.
- **Ice** - on the frozen worlds (**Ida** and **Kamares**) the footing is slippery: you walk **20% slower**.
- **Dikte** - the gas giant is landable too: no ground, only metal **platforms** hovering in its clouds (level decks, undersides toward the sky), linked by **bridges**. No villages up there - **refineries, factories, depots and relay stations** stand on the platforms instead, and pirates roam them. Mind the edges: beyond the railings there is only cloud - the giant's banded cloud deck far below, its belts and zones streaming past in opposite directions, storms and eddies drifting along them.
- **Wildlife** - forest planets like Amnissos teem with Greek animals: Cretan wild goats, deer and hares (shy - they run when you come close), sheep and pack donkeys grazing round the villages, foxes, tortoises (they pull into their shells), little owls that flit off as you approach, and golden eagles circling overhead - and stranger, alien beasts: striped tigrokeros and glowing selas stags (shy), mushroom mammoths and capped slugs plodding about, bubble toads, moss pangolins that roll into a ball, aeromantas gliding overhead and sky jellies drifting at head height - and giant insects: horned scarabs and rhinoceros beetles, mushroom pillbugs and leaf bugs that roll up into balls, peacock moths, lantern fireflies and dragonflies. Hover over one to see what it is. Animals of one kind stick together: hurt one and **the whole group** near it turns on you - even sheep - while a lone small animal runs. Beware the **predators** (red on the minimap like pirates): **wolf packs** and **harpyx raptor** packs hunt you from afar and close in from all sides, **wild boars** and armoured **hoplorhinos** charge if you come near, and **snakes**, **drakaina serpents**, **giant mantises** - and the insect hunters: **jumping spiders**, **giant centipedes**, **stick mantises**, **fungal stalkers** and **glass grubs** - strike if you step too close. Fight them like pirates (click one, or press F); a badly hurt wolf or harpyx runs. Anything that bites you gets shot back at without a click (you can keep walking - or run), and when the one you were fighting falls you turn on the next that's after you. **Hunting**: any animal can be shot - click it - and every fallen animal leaves a chest of **Cybernetic Matter** (more from the big ones), half flesh, half machine, that stations buy as cargo. Big grazers with horns or antlers (goats, stags, the mushroom mammoth, beetles) turn and fight whoever hurts them; the rest run or hide. The wild has its own food chain too: hungry predators hunt the other animals (anything not bigger than they are), the hunted flee, and predators fight back when attacked. Brought down by an animal, you come to beside your ship - it takes no drachmas. The **ice planets** (Ida, Kamares) have crystal beasts of their own: shy crystal stags and frost-winged hares, shard crawlers and star crawlers (they curl up), frost rays gliding overhead and ice wisps drifting about - and hunters: **crystal wolf** packs, the charging **frost behemoth**, long-legged **crystal striders**, **frost scuttlers**, **bubble spiders** and **ice wyrms**.
- Roofs and front walls fade when you're inside or behind them.
- **Leaving** - click your landed ship or right-click > Leave planet: you return to orbit where you were.

## field-computer | The Field Computer | keywords: Field Computer, Bestiary, Inventory, Medicine, Energy cell, toolbar
**Tab** opens your Field Computer on a planet - the pilot's own version of the Ship Computer (the game goes on while it's open; it closes by itself if you're attacked). Its tabs (1-7): **Quest** (the main quest's journal), **Inventory** (**I**: your health, rifle and everything you carry - click medicine or an energy cell to use it), **Repair** (the [Repair Bay](doc:repair-bay): your automaton's parts - and your landed ship's), **Bestiary** (the planet's wildlife: every creature you've come near, how it behaves, how tough it is and how many you've hunted; the ones you haven't met are silhouettes), **Archive** ([every book](doc:archive)), **Map** (the planet map, right in the Field Computer: **M** opens it there) and **Skills** (**K**: the [Spell Book](doc:skills)).

![](shot:field_inventory)

The **toolbar** at the bottom of the screen has **9 slots** (keys **1-9**, or click) you fill yourself: in the Field Computer's inventory **drag** your rifle, medicine or an energy cell onto a slot (or hover it and press **1-9**); drag slots to swap them; right-click a slot to empty it. Drag the stacks you carry to arrange them. At first: **1 Laser rifle** fires at the nearest enemy (like F); **2 Medicine** heals 50 health (one Medicine from what you carry); **3 Energy cell** overcharges the rifle - twice the rate of fire for 10 s (one Energy Cell, then 20 s before the next); **4 Pygmachia**, **5 Hermes' Leap** and **6 Phlox** - your first [skills](doc:skills). Over the bar: your **level** and a thin bar of experience toward the next. The counts are what you carry - take medicine and cells from your ship's hold at the ship.

## skills | Skills: martial arts, the leap and the arcana | keywords: Skills, Spell Book, Pygmachia, Pankration, Laktisma, Scythe Sweep, Comet Kick, Aspis Guard, Hermes' Leap, Helios Lance, Phlox, Keraunos, Aegis Dome, Eidola, skill point, level, experience, rank, Learn
On foot your automaton is more than a rifle: it fights with its **fists and feet**, **leaps** across a fight, and commands the **arcana** - beams, fire, lightning, a dome of force, spectral fighters. Skills go on the **toolbar** (keys **1-9**) like anything else; the **Spell Book** - the Field Computer's **Skills** tab, **K** - is where you learn them and raise their ranks.

![](shot:skill_book)
- **Levels** - fighting earns **experience**: enemies you defeat (the tougher, the more), blows and spells that land. Each **level** (to 20) gives a **skill point**; the bar over the toolbar shows how far the next is. In the Spell Book a point **learns** a skill (each needs a level: its row says which) or **raises its rank** (to 5): more damage (+20% a rank), shorter cooldowns, and what its rank lines say - a longer chain, a wider burst, another eidolon. Hover a skill to read it in full on the right. A learned skill goes onto a free toolbar slot; drag its icon to another, or hover it and press **1-9**.
- **Stamina** - every skill costs some (a blow about 1, a spell 5-12): eat and drink to keep fighting ([stamina](doc:planets)). Techniques and spells also have a **cooldown** (the dark curtain on their slot).
- **Martial styles** - a style is how you fight when you attack: use it from the toolbar (or click an enemy while it's your style - its slot is marked) and the automaton runs up and works through the style's **chain of blows**, one after the other, until the enemy falls or you click away. Blows **stagger** (the enemy can't act for a moment), kicks **shove**, finishers **floor** them (they lie there, then get up). Slot 1, the rifle, goes back to shooting.
  - **Pygmachia** (the boxer's art, from the start): jab, cross - then a hook (rank 2) and an uppercut that floors (rank 3). Fast and cheap.
  - **Pankration** (level 2): elbow, knee - then a front kick that drives them back (rank 2) and a force palm that throws them (rank 3).
  - **Laktisma** (level 4): side kick and a roundhouse that hits **everyone in front of you** - then a spinning back kick (rank 3).
- **Techniques** - **Aspis Guard** (level 2): arms up for a moment - most of what hits you is shrugged off. **Scythe Sweep** (level 5): a low spinning sweep that floors everyone around you. **Comet Kick** (level 7): a flying kick across the gap (340 px and more) onto an enemy.
- **Hermes' Leap** (from the start) - a flip through the air to **where the mouse points** (up to 380 px, further with ranks; not through walls). Use it to close on a rifleman, to get out of a crossfire or over a pack of wolves: **shots fired at you while you're in the air miss**. From rank 3 the landing staggers those around.

![](shot:skills_fight)
- **The arcana** - aimed at the enemy under the mouse (else the one you're fighting, else the nearest; with none, at the spot the mouse points to):
  - **Phlox** (from the start): a ball of fire that bursts where it lands - everyone within its burst is hit and left **burning** for 4 seconds.
  - **Helios Lance** (level 3): a beam from your palms, through **everything in its line** up to 720 px (walls stop it).
  - **Keraunos** (level 6): a thunderbolt from the sky that stuns its target and **leaps on** to others near at half strength - one more a rank.
  - **Aegis Dome** (level 8): a dome around you that throws back those standing close and **soaks up damage** (60, more with ranks) until it breaks or its time runs out.
  - **Eidola** (level 10): spectral fighters - pale copies of yourself - rise out of the ground and go for your enemies with fists and feet for 18 seconds and more; pirates shoot at them as at anyone. One at first, two at rank 3, three at rank 5.
- **On a gamepad** skills are aimed the way you face. Everything works with the **classic sprites** too (Settings > Characters drawn from: the original hand-drawn pictures of the automaton and the pirates, kept as a backup) - the blows and spells just happen without their animations.

## surface-map | The planet map | keywords: Close the map, Reset view, Layers
**M** shows the whole planet - the Field Computer's Map tab (a teleport gate opens the portal network's own map): you, your ship, every village's buildings and the citizens and pirates near you - in the parts you've explored. **Fog of war**: the planet map and the minimap are dark where you haven't been; walking reveals the land round you (about 44 tiles), and the villages and people there appear. Each planet remembers what you've seen. The wheel zooms (far in: the planet is big; a middle click: the whole planet again), dragging pans, and clicking a spot walks you there - a long way off, you set out toward it and keep going until you arrive. It's drawn like a console's terrain map in the interface's amber: glowing pale-amber coastlines, the land hillshaded, **orange routes** from your ship to each settlement (dotted pale ones between them), circled icons for the settlements (a temple for the palace), your ship and pirates (red warnings), a compass and a scale bar. The **Layers** panel turns routes, places, people and the grid on and off, and the planet's card sits in the corner.

![](shot:surface_map)


**Teleport gates** - glowing Minoan portal arches stand across every planet: one by the landing pad, one by every village and a few out in the wilds. Click one (walk up to it) and the **portal network** opens - the map with every gate on the planet, linked from the one you're at; click any other gate and you step out in front of it at once.
